posts.title: Bab n Yids, Dadda Yids
posts.contentHtml:
As a small child in a town tucked into the Anti-Atlas mountains, crying on my mother’s back as she tried to lull me to sleep, nothing etched itself into my memory more deeply than the tender old lullaby Bab n Yids.

Our Version of the Lullaby, Bab n Yids

Nmaggarkh Bab n Yids Innayi Matrbit

ⵏⵎⴰⴳⴳⴰⵔⵅ ⴱⴰⴱ ⵏ ⵢⵉⴷⵙ ⵉⵏⵏⴰⵢⵉ ⵎⴰⵜⵔⴱⵉⵜ

I met the god of sleep, and he asked me, Who are you carrying ( on your back )?”

Nnighas Ya’ Wwazzan, Innayi Snuhnnut.

ⵏⵏⵉⵖⴰⵙ ⵢⴰ’ⵡⵡⴰⵣⵣⴰⵏ, ⵉⵏⵏⴰⵢⵉ ⵙⵏⵓⵀⵏⵏⵓⵜ

I told him a little kid, and he told me, “lull him.”

Snuhnnut Snuhnnut, Snuhnnut Snuhnnut.

ⵙⵏⵓⵀⵏⵏⵓⵜ ⵙⵏⵓⵀⵏⵏⵓⵜ, ⵙⵏⵓⵀⵏⵏⵓⵜ ⵙⵏⵓⵀⵏⵏⵓⵜ.

lull him lull him, lull him lull him

Nuhnnu, Nuhnnu, Nuhnnu, Nuhnnu

ⵏⵓⵀⵏⵏⵓ ⵏⵓⵀⵏⵏⵓ, ⵏⵓⵀⵏⵏⵓ ⵏⵓⵀⵏⵏⵓ.

Sleep Sleep, Sleep Sleep.

Listen on youtube

An Alternative Version, Dadda Yids

Nmaggarkh Dadda Yids Innayi Matrbit

I met my lord Sleep, and he asked me, Who are you carrying ( on your back )?”

Innayi Matribit, Nnighas Ayyur

He asked me, “Who are you babysitting?” I told him Ayyur ( Moon )

Immudda Wayyur, Nnighas Manza Lhdert

Ayyur is gone. I asked him where the party was

Innayi han lhdert, han lhdert, dar mdn an

He told me, “There it is, there it is, with those people.”

A Rbikhk ay’Ayyur ar Fttukh ar Allakh

Oh, Moon, I’m carrying you, walking and crying

Yaghk Lazz ay’Ayyur Imun dis Wala Ids

You’re hungry, and you’re sleepy

Yaghk Lazza Wala Ids Yili Osmmid gh ichnran

You’re hungry, and you’re sleepy with cold lips

Nmaggarkh Dadda Yids Innayi Matrbit

I met my lord Sleep, and he asked me, Who are you carrying

Nnighas Mad Rbikh Dadda Yids Ya’Wayyur

I told him who I’m carrying, my lord, a Moon!

Innayi Snuhnnut, Snuhnnut, Snuhnnut

He told me, lull him, lull him, lull him

nuhnnu nuhnnu nuhnnu nuhnnu

Sleep, Sleep, Sleep, Sleep

posts.title: Noursletter 05 - Content is a cursed word!
posts.summary: Don't make content, or at least don't call it that!
posts.contentHtml:
Hello again! 👋

Firstly, thank you for all your kind responses to my last email. Welcome if you’re a new subscriber and cheers if you’ve been here for a while, I hope you’re having a good end of the year, holiday season, or some good world cup days if you’re into football.

Why you should stop using the word “content”?

The word "content" has become associated with low-quality or spammy material that is created solely for the purpose of generating clicks and attention, rather than providing value or engaging with the audience.

Using the word "content" can make the material being referred to sound generic and uninteresting. Instead of using a vague term like "content," it may be more effective to use specific words that accurately describe the type of material being presented, such as "article," "video," or "podcast."

Make Art Not Content.. a podcast I listen to!

Latest Tweets

I made these for the love of Atay ( Moroccan Tea ).

Quote of the Week

"The word 'content' is just a label we put on things to make them seem less valuable than they actually are. It's like when you go to a yard sale and everything is labeled 'junk.'" -

posts.title: Noursletter 04 - Start Tiny, Make Many, Celebrate Often!
posts.summary: A way to love creating again
posts.contentHtml:
Welcome to all the new subscribers this week. Thanks for joining!

We are a little more than 300 now, and I’m happy to see you all here. I’ll make sure to keep you updated on the newsletter growth every now and then.

Start tiny!

Whether it’s writing a book, picking a skill, learning a new language, or simply cleaning your house, projects often seem larger in our brains than they are in reality.

“Far too often, we don’t start because we can’t get our minds around the entire thing. We don’t take the first step because we can’t figure out the seventeenth step. But you don’t have to know the seventeenth step. You only have to know the first step…Start with 1.” -Rob Bell

Here’s Why Starting Small Works

It builds your habit of execution ⚙️

You can probably write three articles in a single day if you try, but it will drain you, and your brain will reject doing it again.

Instead what you want to do is grow into the habit and train your writing muscles.

one or two paragraphs a day until doing that feels smooth then increase the number. not just writing, this is true for almost everything. 

It makes you practice and fine-tune your craft 🛠️

You'll learn what works for you and what doesn't, and you'll be more efficient in your process.

You get immediate feedback on what’s working and what’s not 💬

By creating small ideas and sharing them with people you receive fast feedback, and you get to know what sticks so you can double down on it.

You build your confidence as a maker 🛡️

Every time you finish a small idea, you feel accomplished. you feel proud of yourself. Because you are doing what you said, you are — a maker! ( designer, writer...)

Make Many

As Daniel Vassallo always says, build a "portfolio of small bets".

Ship something small with value, and ship it fast, and don't waste your time on hugely ambitious projects that require a ton of willpower. 

"More shots, less moonshots, It's much easier to double down on something that already works than working blind-fully on a moonshot project." —Ben Issen

Celebrate often!

Celebrate small wins to celebrate often, and give yourself the credit that you deserve, nothing more, nothing less.

The feeling of accomplishment is what will give you the power to continue.

Quote of the Week

Start by doing what’s necessary; then do what’s possible; and suddenly you are doing the impossible.

- Francis of Assisi

posts.title: Noursletter 03 - Amazigh inspiration!
posts.summary: Our roots are our source of creativity
posts.contentHtml:
As a north African born and raised Amazigh, it only makes sense that I should look for inspiration in my native culture.

I grew up speaking the language and living the full Amazigh lifestyle in a small mountain town south of morocco. listening and dancing to the music, eating the local food, and celebrating the traditions.

the Amazigh creative output was all around me, from the clothes and jewelry to the pots and textiles, so I would say I’m somewhat familiar with the art in my region but that’s only one part of the Amazigh world, and I need to discover the rest.

#Artmazigh Day Reconnects Amazigh Artists to Showcase their Heritage

is there a better place to look for other people that share your same interest than Twitter?

well, it’s where I started to look and found this gem #Artmazigh . a hashtag for Amazigh artists to showcase their Heritage using art, scroll down the feed and you’re in for an eye pleasing experience.

Book: Amazigh Arts in Morocco Women Shaping Berber Identity

a book by Cynthia Becker about the role of women in shaping the Amazigh identity.

get the book as a PDF here.

The Amazigh music between the folklore, the classics, and the modern wave

You can’t hear the Amazigh music without getting attracted, amazed, or even attached.

I grew up with the folklore (Ahwach) and the classics (Rways, Tagroupit) and I lived to see our music evolve, so here I share with you two Amazigh playlists that I made and listen to on Spotify.

The first is a playlist for the love of Izenzaren, my favorite Amazigh band growing up.

The second is a collection of songs by young talented artists that are trying to modernize the Amazigh music.

Say hello!

Thank you for reading. I always love hearing from people and if you enjoyed this, please reach out by replying to this email or you can find me on Twitter @nouroumousse

posts.title: Noursletter 02 - Writing, Bookmarking & Consuming content!
posts.contentHtml:
A purpose to write

This newsletter is intended to help me articulate my ideas and views better by putting them into words, and in the meantime share them with people, and hopefully get some feedback.

My aim is to see how much I actually know about the things that I think I know and learn from that in the process.

“ You can know a great deal about something without writing about it.

Can you ever know so much that you wouldn't learn more from trying to explain what you know? I don't think so. ” — Paul Graham

Article

After starting this newsletter my consumption of articles and blog posts increased drastically, trying to see how fellow creators write and what they’re writing about.

and after one week of discovery, I’m amazed at how some people write extremely well and I love how Paco Coursey put it:

"We all use the same set of words, but some writers are so much better at using them." —— Paco Coursey

Article

Consuming content

I was rarely reading articles before starting this, maybe 4 to 5 a week but now I consume the same amount or more daily. driven by wanting to write but also by discovering a useful tip to consume more easily!

isn’t it just easier to listen than stare at white screens for too long?

so here are some tools to help you with that:

Google translate voice

it’s the first one I started using, good enough and does the job. copy and paste into the English box, click the speaker and start listening.

NaturalReaders

a great tool with a better voice than the one in google translate but its free plan is limited

Speechify

better service than NaturalReaders, better voices on the premium plan, and it is also the one Medium integrated into their articles.

My beloved Siri

it’s what I use now and honestly, it’s good as it can be. select text and click Option+Esc and enjoy!

you can also change the voice from the accessibility settings.

Bookmarking

bookmark first and read later? no! I prefer to bookmark things I already tasted and found interesting

you can follow my internet bookmarks here

I use Mymind extension and app to bookmark, but Pocket is a great one as well.

Say hello!

I always love hearing from people and if you enjoyed this, please reach out! You can find me on Twitter @nouroumousse

posts.title: Noursletter 01 - The first of many
posts.contentHtml:
Welcome to the first email! I’ll be honest, I’m very new to this but I always wanted some kind of online journal.

It may be either a weekly one or once every two weeks, mainly because I hate forcing stuff, I’ve always been one to share things when they come naturally to me.

Who am I and what do I do?

I’m Nour, a 25 years old skinny tall guy from the south of Morocco. I’ve been in the creative industry since 2016, but my obsession with the field started way earlier. from drawing cartoon characters to exploring every creative software I got my hands on as a kid.

My professional journey started by learning the basics of Adobe Illustrator and how to make logos with it, and I used Dribbble as my main portfolio and source of traffic to get clients.

I managed to build some traction around my work and that helped me sustain a stream of design leads coming to my inbox every month.

Dribbble quite literally transformed my life, I have never sold a gig on Fiverr nor won a contest on 99design, and never worked on a freelance platform either, it was all from Dribbble at some point.

My business was built from the start on direct interaction with the client by email mainly with no need for a third-party platform.

A few things I’ve learned along the way

Consistency beats all

As cliche as it sounds, it’s the hard truth. you’ll never get consistent results if you didn’t put consistent effort into anything.

build systems, stick to them, get feedback, and iterate!

Clients chose people they know first

Clients are people and people chose familiarity. so make sure you put yourself in the market and build relationships before even mentioning any business.

Dribbble alternatives that worked for me and some I'm still exploring

Twitter Design Community

I’m not talking here about the “Twitter communities” new feature, but about the design community on Twitter as a whole.

A great place to get feedback, network, and land clients as well.

Linkedin

Like Twitter but in a more formal way, you can share your work consistently on Linkedin and you’d be surprised by the results.

Behance

Behance is the old guy in town for designers, but the platform still holds some of its value, mainly because of the curation system implemented.

With a little bit of strategy, it can become a good source of design leads for you.

Explore Family

A new minimalistic-looking platform for creatives that aims to fix some of the major issues in the classic ones like Dribbble and Behance.

Layers.to

An indie project that cut my eye and I loved its simplicity so I joined.

I’ll keep sharing other alternatives in this thread on Twitter

Bookmarks of the week

buttons I'd like to press — Are.na

mymind is the extension for your mind.

Neal.fun - fun internet stuff

What can I do for you?

Please leave any comments, thoughts, and questions. I’m always looking for new topics to cover and I’ll answer everyone.

Anything I could help you with, don’t hesitate to reply to this email or reach out to me on Twitter, my DMs are always open.

Thanks for reading Noursletter! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
